distractors.reason: 'Free work' is not the standard phrase. 'Free' means it costs nothing to the customer, while 'unpaid' means the worker receives no salary.
'Empty work' has no meaning in this context. 'Empty' describes a space or container that holds nothing.
'Cheap work' suggests low quality or a low price. It does not describe work that is done without pay.

example_sentence: She spent the summer doing ___ work at a local food bank.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden traducir 'trabajo gratis' como 'free work', pero en inglés se dice 'unpaid work'. 'Free' se usa para cosas sin costo, no para trabajo sin salario.
explanation: In English, 'unpaid' is the adjective used to describe work that a person does without receiving any money, such as volunteer work. 'Unpaid' is the natural choice for this idea.

related_collocations.example: He has a part-time job at a bookshop on weekends.
After school she wants a full-time job in a hospital.
Many students do voluntary work to help their community.

memory_tip: UNPAID = no salary (unpaid work, unpaid leave) | FREE = costs nothing for the customer (free entry, free sample)
